items.title: Russia says at least seven killed in largest Ukrainian attack of 2026
items.description: Moscow also launched deadly strikes against Ukraine overnight, sparking fires across the capital Kyiv.

items.title: Thousands displaced by deadly Indonesia earthquake as rescue efforts continue
items.description: Hundreds of homes and public buildings have been severely damaged with at least 53 people killed.

items.title: Hurricane Lala sparks flash floods in Hawaii as strong winds and rain persist
items.description: Officials say flash flooding may have swept away homes with people in them in worst-hit areas.

items.title: Twelve killed as Polish bus veers off Hungarian motorway
items.description: Dozens more are seriously injured after the tourist bus overturned in the early hours of Sunday morning.

items.title: Europe's tallest Virgin Mary statue unveiled in rural Poland
items.description: The 55.6-metre (182ft) concrete figure is head-and-shoulders above Rio de Jaineiro's Christ the Redeemer.

items.title: Belgian wildfire doubles in size on third day tearing through nature reserve
items.description: Hundreds of firefighters are trying to contain the flames consuming the major park.

items.title: Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots after downing fighter jets
items.description: Iran claims they have been held since Qatar downed two fighter jets at the start of the US-Iran war.

items.title: Four 'extraordinary' Renaissance paintings stolen from Italian museum
items.description: The works were taken overnight without alarms being triggered, raising suspicion of a professional hit.

items.title: Morocco detains dozens of migrants trying to cross into Ceuta, reports say
items.description: Security had been stepped up amid suggestions on social media of a second mass crossing on Saturday.

items.title: Liechtenstein changes succession rule to allow women to ascend the throne
items.description: The declaration was made on the national day of the central European country, which has a population of just 44,000.

items.title: Teenager arrested in Virginia State University shooting that injured five
items.description: The 19-year-old, who was not a student at the university, was found hiding in a closet on campus, according to police.

items.title: Eleven killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, authorities say
items.description: Israel's military said it had struck "Hezbollah terror infrastructure" in response to what it described as earlier action against its soldiers.

items.title: Australian state to launch gun buyback after Bondi Beach attack
items.description: New South Wales, where the attack took place, will offer gun owners cash to give up their firearms.

items.title: Family stranded at sea for 16 hours after jet ski capsized in Thailand
items.description: A father and his two young sons spent a night adrift before being rescued off the coast of the island of Koh Samui.

items.title: BBC seeks to subpoena family members in Panorama lawsuit
items.description: A spokesperson for Trump's legal team responded to the request accusing the broadcaster of "seeking to harass" the president's family.

items.title: South Korea proposes talks to officially end war with North
items.description: Lee Jae Myung offers chance to end the conflict, which has been frozen since an armistice in 1953.

items.title: France's top court blocks social media ban for under-15s
items.description: The Constitutional Council says it infringes upon freedom of expression - but President Macron vows to prepare a new draft.

items.title: US aircraft carrier on way to relieve USS Lincoln after issues reported aboard
items.description: Thousands of sailors on the Lincoln have reportedly faced food shortages and broken plumbing, with some considering jumping overboard.

items.title: Many Canadians are boycotting the US, so this is where they're travelling instead
items.description: From exploring their own backyard to travelling abroad, many Canadians are spending their money elsewhere to send a message to the US president.

items.title: Five years after the Taliban swept to power, does the West have any influence?
items.description: Five years after the Taliban swept to power, many are asking whether the West has any bargaining chips left
